CausalChain: NAFLD-induced metabolic stress -> Upregulation of FTO (modulated by other m6A regulators ALKBH5, WTAP) -> FTO (with co-regulatory partners) performs selective removal of m6A marks on lipid metabolism-regulating RNAs -> Increased stability and translation of these transcripts -> Altered lipogenesis and metabolic reprogramming -> In the presence of additional oncogenic signals (e.g., RNF5 pathway) and overcoming compensatory ncRNA feedback -> Context-dependent malignant transformation of hepatocytes -> Development of HCC
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that NAFLD-induced metabolic stress activates signaling pathways that upregulate FTO and concurrently modulate the activity of other m6A regulators such as ALKBH5 and WTAP. This results in a selective, motif-driven removal of m6A modifications from a defined subset of mRNAs and specific noncoding RNAs involved in lipid metabolism. The ensuing stabilization and enhanced translation of these transcripts promote altered lipogenesis and metabolic reprogramming. When hepatocytes experience a secondary boost from additional oncogenic mechanisms—for instance, a RNF5-mediated pathway triggered by fatty acid excess—the integrated epitranscriptomic modifications and metabolic reprogramming exceed a critical threshold, thereby priming these cells for malignant transformation and HCC development. Our approach will employ advanced technologies including single-nucleotide resolution m6A mapping, CRISPR-based modulation of FTO and its co-regulators, ribosome profiling, and integrative machine-learning analysis to resolve the temporal and functional interplay of these events.
Abstract: Non‐alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) generates metabolic stress that not only upregulates the m6A demethylase FTO but also modulates a broader epitranscriptomic network including regulators such as ALKBH5 and WTAP. We propose that under NAFLD conditions, increased FTO expression—potentially through defined signaling pathways—leads to a highly selective removal of m6A modifications from a particular subset of mRNAs and noncoding RNAs that are enriched for motifs regulating lipid metabolism. This selective demethylation enhances the stability and translational efficiency of these transcripts, thereby driving altered lipogenesis and broader metabolic reprogramming. Critically, this FTO‐driven epitranscriptomic reprogramming does not act in isolation; its effects are modulated by compensatory activities within the m6A machinery and by context‐dependent noncoding RNA networks. In a subset of hepatocytes, particularly when additional oncogenic pathways (such as a RNF5‐mediated axis responsive to fatty acid excess) are concurrently activated, these events converge to prime these cells for malignant transformation, ultimately contributing to the development of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We will leverage single-nucleotide resolution m6A mapping, CRISPR-based modulation, ribosome profiling, and advanced machine learning analytics on high-throughput sequencing datasets to dissect the temporal kinetics and interplay of these molecular events.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis centered on NAFLD-induced FTO upregulation leading to selective m6A demethylation of lipid regulatory transcripts and subsequent metabolic reprogramming predisposing hepatocytes to transformation. In the revised version, we have maintained these core elements but expanded the scope to explicitly include: (1) the detailed involvement of additional m6A regulators (ALKBH5, WTAP) in modulating FTO’s actions, (2) the concept of selective, motif- and structure-driven demethylation to address the specificity of the process, (3) the integration of parallel oncogenic signals such as the RNF5 axis that may synergize with FTO-driven events, and (4) the practical implementation of advanced technological approaches (e.g., machine learning-enhanced analysis of high-throughput data) to improve experimental resolution and validation of the causal chain.
